newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi optimistic on economic recovery.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi optimistic on economic recovery.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in an interview released on Monday that he was optimistic about Italy's economic recovery after difficult deficit-reduction measures of the past year.

In an interview in the American weekly magazine Time, Prodi restated his longstanding position that he would feel compelled to resign if Italy did not become part of the European single currency from the outset.
"The country suffered but the fact is that the economic system performed much better than expected under these conditions," he said.
"Of course the rate of growth was low, but we didn't kill the country. So I am optimistic concerning the recovery.
"The next step is to make long-range corrections, particularly in reining in the welfare state," he said.
Prodi also that he was confident Italy would meet strict parameters in the Maastricht treaty to allow the country to join the European single currency from the outset.
He said Italians knew that joining European monetary union was "a battle that counts for centuries" and repeated the consequences of failing to join would be huge.
"You would have an attack on the lira, devaluation. All the sacrifices we've made would be nullified.

"Second, the country would be demoralised. Third, there is the club effect: once the club is formed, the price of entry will be higher and higher. Finally, as I have repeatedly said, I would feel compelled to resign."
